STA Hubs - Codebase & Maintenance Guide

How the two internal hub apps are built, and exactly how to change and deploy them  ·  Adam Baker  ·  Updated 2026-07-06

INTERNAL · ADMIN REFERENCE

What this is: the maintenance manual for STA's two internal hub apps - the AI Training Hub and the STA Support Hub. It covers how each is built, where the code lives, how to make a change, and how to deploy it safely.

Who it's for: whoever maintains the hubs (today: Adam). You do not need to be a developer to follow the change procedures - they're copy-paste steps.

The one thing to remember: both apps are single self-contained files with no build step. You edit one file, sync a mirror copy, and open a pull request. That's the whole loop.

Why single-file, no buildBoth apps embed their data in a JavaScript object inside one HTML file. No npm install, no compile, no toolchain to break. Anyone can open the file, edit a data entry, and the change is live after a sync and push. That simplicity is deliberate - keep it.

AI Training Hub - how the code works

The entire app is STA-Training-Hub.html. Everything staff see is driven by one JavaScript object, window.TRAINING_DATA, which has two parts:

window.TRAINING_DATA = {
  audiences: [            // the tabs across the top
    { id:'admin', title:'AI Admin', icon:'...', sub:'...',
      sections: [          // headings within a tab
        { heading:'System reference', docs:['system-overview', ...] }
      ] }
  ],
  docs: {                 // one entry per card, referenced by id
    'system-overview': {
      title:'...', desc:'...(<= ~200 chars / 5 lines)',
      file:'docs/system-overview.html', type:'html',
      priority:'admin', tags:['Admin','Reference'],
      added:'2026-06-06', updated:'2026-06-06'
    }
  }
};
  • Audiences = tabs. Array order = tab order. Current tabs: Start Here, Sales, Support, Marketing, Operations, Renewals, Salesforce Admins, AI Admin.
  • Sections = headings inside a tab, each listing card ids in docs:[...].
  • One doc id, many tabs. The same card can appear on several tabs - it's defined once in docs{} and referenced from each tab's docs:[...].
  • The card opens a real file in dist/docs/ (HTML/MD) or dist/files/ (docx/pptx/pdf). No content is rendered inside the app - it's a launcher.
  • Priority sets the card color: required = blue, recommended = green, optional = gray, admin = orange.

The dist/ folder is what Cloudflare actually serves: dist/index.html (a copy of the source file), dist/docs/ (all HTML/markdown docs), and dist/files/ (source Word/PowerPoint files, which convert-docx-to-html.py turns into styled HTML in dist/docs/).

AI Training Hub - how to make a change

Add a new doc / card

  1. Name the file as a kebab-case slug - lowercase, hyphens, no spaces (e.g. customer-renewal-workflow.html). Spaces silently break Cloudflare uploads.
  2. Put the file in dist. HTML/markdown → dist/docs/; Word/PowerPoint/PDF → dist/files/ (then run python3 convert-docx-to-html.py your-slug.docx to generate the served HTML).
  3. Add a docs{} entry in STA-Training-Hub.html. Use an id matching the slug; keep desc to ~200 chars (cards clamp at 5 lines).
  4. Reference the id from one or more audiences[].sections[].docs arrays - this is what makes the card appear on a tab.
  5. Sync + deploy (see the deploy section below).
AI Admin card placement is a hard ruleAn agent/tool card goes in a bucket by its registry Deployment Target: Claude.ai Projects on top, Coworks below, built web apps under System reference. Check context-agent-registry.md first - never guess, never use one mixed "agents & tools" list. Full rule in the hub's MAINTENANCE.md.

Edit or remove a doc

  • Edit text on a card: change the title/desc/tags in the docs{} entry. Edit the doc's content in its dist/docs/*.html file.
  • Edit a Word-derived doc: edit the .docx in dist/files/, then re-run convert-docx-to-html.py. Never hand-edit the generated HTML - it gets overwritten.
  • Remove a doc: delete its docs{} entry, remove the id from every tab's docs:[...], and delete the asset file. Then sync + deploy.

STA Support Hub - how the code works

The Support Hub (repo sta-help-center-index) is the article-index portal for support staff, and also hosts the Project Tracker tab. It is a single-file React app loaded through Babel Standalone - still no build step, just React compiled in the browser.

  • Source of truth is NOT the repo. You edit HC-Index-App.html in the Help Center Assistant project folder (Documents\Claude\Projects\.STA Projects\Help Center Assistant\article-index\). The repo's index.html is the deployed copy, synced from that source.
  • Data lives in window.HC_DATA embedded in the file - Salesforce Knowledge links, internal articles, and email templates organized by product tab. Same "data-in-a-JS-object" pattern as the Training Hub.
  • It's an installable PWA. manifest.json + sw.js (service worker) provide offline caching and "Add to Home Screen." sw.js must stay at the repo root - a service worker only controls its own folder and below.
  • Cache busting: the CACHE constant in sw.js (sta-hc-YYYYMMDD) must be bumped on every deploy or returning users keep the old cached build.

STA Support Hub - how to make a change

  1. Edit the source - HC-Index-App.html in the Help Center Assistant project folder (update window.HC_DATA for content, or the React components for behavior).
  2. Re-sync the repo copy - copy the edited source over index.html in the sta-help-center-index repo (see that project's MAINTENANCE.md for the exact command).
  3. Bump the cache - set CACHE in sw.js to today's date, sta-hc-YYYYMMDD.
  4. Keep root clean - only index.html, manifest.json, sw.js, and dotfiles belong at root. New icons → icons/, CSS → css/, JS → js/.
  5. Branch, PR, merge - same protected-main flow as the Training Hub (below). Cloudflare auto-deploys on merge.
Content ownerThe Support Hub's content and hub source edits are owned by the Help Center Advisor agent (it maintains both internal hubs and hands off a Code-tab/PR prompt - it never pushes). Route content-strategy and article-index work there.

Deploy - the loop that actually ships

Editing a file on disk changes nothing that staff see. Cloudflare Pages deploys from origin/main on GitHub, and main is branch-protected on both repos (CodeRabbit reviews Training Hub PRs; it skips the Support Hub - see below). So the loop is: sync the mirror, branch, open a PR, wait for the required checks, review, merge. The merge is the deploy.

AI Training Hub - sync then PR

# 1. Sync the deployed mirror (byte-identical to source)
cp "STA-Training-Hub.html" "dist/index.html"

# 2. Branch + open a PR (paste into Claude Code / Code tab)
cd "C:\Users\Adam\source\repos\training-kit-hub"
git checkout main && git pull origin main
git checkout -b hub-sync-short-description
git status
git add -- STA-Training-Hub.html dist/index.html   # name the files; never git add -A
git commit -m "concrete message naming what changed"
git push -u origin hub-sync-short-description
gh pr create --base main --fill

# 3. Wait for the required checks to finish
gh pr checks hub-sync-short-description --watch

# 4. Review, then merge. THE MERGE IS WHAT DEPLOYS.
gh pr merge hub-sync-short-description --squash --delete-branch
git checkout main && git pull origin main
Merging is a separate, deliberate stepPushing a branch deploys nothing. Cloudflare Pages deploys on the merge to origin/main, and main is protected - so shipping always costs a branch, a pull request, and a merge you perform yourself after the checks pass. A pushed branch that never merges is the dominant way a hub change silently fails to reach staff. Never merge while a required check is failing or pending, and never disable a check to force one through.
Never do these
  • git push origin main - rejected; main is protected on every BwB repo.
  • git add -A - stages whatever else happens to be in the tree. Both CLAUDE.md and MAINTENANCE.md forbid it. Name the paths: git add -- STA-Training-Hub.html dist/index.html.
  • gh pr merge --squash --auto - auto-merge closes the PR before CodeRabbit finishes and discards the review. Split create from merge.
  • Adding a _redirects file with /* /index.html 200 - Cloudflare rejects the wildcard SPA fallback ([code: 10021] Infinite loop). Neither app needs it.
  • Filenames with spaces - Cloudflare drag-and-drop uploads silently fail mid-batch. Kebab-case slugs only.
CodeRabbit silence is NOT a pass - on either repoCodeRabbit skips these repos, reporting the check as passed with the message "Review skipped: manual review required for this OSS repository." A green CodeRabbit check therefore means nobody reviewed the diff - not that it came back clean. Confirmed on both repos: the Support Hub (sta-help-center-index) was already known to skip, and the Training Hub was observed doing the same on PR #45 (2026-08-17), so the earlier belief that the Training Hub still got a real automated review is wrong. Read the diff yourself before merging either one. The required checks - not CodeRabbit - are what actually gate the merge.

Support Hub - same flow, plus cache bump

Identical branch→PR→squash-merge on the sta-help-center-index repo, with one extra step: bump CACHE in sw.js before committing, or returning PWA users keep the stale cached build. After merge, confirm the deploy in a fresh private window.

Gotchas & quick troubleshooting

SymptomCause & fix
Card opens a 404The asset isn't in dist/docs/ or dist/files/. Check docs[id].file matches the real filename.
Edit didn't show up on the live hubEither the dist mirror wasn't synced (cp step) or the PR wasn't merged. No merge = no deploy.
Whole Training Hub is blankJS syntax error in the inline module script. Open the browser console - it names the line (no Babel step to hide it).
Support Hub shows old content after deployCACHE in sw.js wasn't bumped. Set it to today's sta-hc-YYYYMMDD, redeploy, reload in a private window.
A .md/.docx card won't open (others fine)Those two lazy-load pinned libraries (marked/mammoth) with SRI hashes. If a hash is stale the browser blocks it - regenerate per DEPLOY.md.
Users stuck on repeated Cloudflare loginThird-party cookies blocked. Enable them for cloudflareaccess.com or try another browser.
A deploy broke the appCloudflare Pages → Deployments → roll back to the last good one (~10 sec).
Full detail lives in the reposThis guide is the map. The authoritative step-by-step is in each repo: Training Hub - MAINTENANCE.md + DEPLOY.md; Support Hub - README.md + CLAUDE.md + the Help Center Assistant project's MAINTENANCE.md.
